standard_prerequisites.name: A presentation of the algebra by a polynomial algebra over the base gives a two-term complex computing the naive cotangent complex, with the conormal module in degree -1
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the explicit complex whose base change is compared, and expresses the tor amplitude condition through the flatness of the conormal module.

standard_prerequisites.name: For a flat algebra the kernel of the base changed presentation is the tensor product of the original kernel with the new base ring
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the conormal module of the base changed presentation with the base change of the original one, which gives the isomorphism of complexes.

standard_prerequisites.name: A two-term complex whose degree zero term is free has tor amplitude in the interval from minus one to zero exactly when its degree minus one term is flat, so the derived tensor product coincides with the ordinary one
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the ordinary base change isomorphism into a derived one under the tor amplitude hypothesis.

core_obligations: Choose a presentation of the algebra over the base by a polynomial algebra, let the kernel of the presentation be the conormal module, and form the corresponding presentation of the base changed algebra (proof lines 22825-22828).

Use flatness of the algebra over the base to identify the kernel of the base changed presentation with the tensor product of the original kernel with the new base ring, and compute the conormal module of the base changed presentation as the tensor product over the algebra of the original conormal module with the new base (proof lines 22828-22836).

Compare modules of differentials: the differentials of the base changed polynomial algebra are the base change of the differentials of the original one because both have the same basis, so the comparison map of the naive cotangent complexes is an isomorphism of complexes, which gives the first statement (proof lines 22836-22842).

For the second statement, write the naive cotangent complex as a two-term complex with the conormal module in degree minus one and the differentials in degree zero, observe that it has tor amplitude in the interval from minus one to zero exactly when the conormal module is flat, and conclude that the derived tensor product coincides with the ordinary one, so the comparison remains a quasi-isomorphism (proof lines 22844-22852).
proof_roadmap: Choose a polynomial presentation and compute the conormal modules of the original and the base changed presentation using flatness (proof lines 22825-22836).
Identify the differentials and conclude that the comparison map of naive cotangent complexes is an isomorphism (proof lines 22836-22842).
Reinterpret the tor amplitude hypothesis as flatness of the conormal module and upgrade the ordinary base change to a derived one (proof lines 22844-22852).
difficulty_reason: The statement concerns a cocartesian square of rings and says that if the algebra is flat over the base then the base change of its naive cotangent complex is a quasi-isomorphism onto the naive cotangent complex of the base changed algebra, and that the derived version holds as well when the naive cotangent complex has tor amplitude in the interval from minus one to zero (statement lines 22809-22823). The proof chooses a polynomial presentation, uses flatness to identify the kernels of the two presentations and hence the conormal modules, compares the modules of differentials to get an isomorphism of complexes, and then observes that a two-term complex whose degree zero term is free has the stated tor amplitude exactly when its conormal module is flat, which makes the ordinary and derived tensor products agree (proof lines 22825-22852). The identification of the conormal module under base change is what carries the argument.
